Overview

Join us for a fun workshop!

Hop on your bike and follow Thomas, who has ridden La Vélodyssée twice, along France’s Atlantic coast from the Basque Country to Brittany.

We’ll travel stage by stage. Along the way, you’ll learn about the history of cycle touring in France and see how the landscapes change from one region to the next. We’ll stop at towns, villages and local landmarks, with cultural and historical stories at each one. Every stage also comes with a tasting of regional specialities.

Stages: the Basque Country · Landes & Gironde · Brittany & Loire-Atlantique

🗯️ French A2/B1 level required
🗓️ Saturday, 28 November 2026, 11.30am–1pm

long_description:
Overview

Hono mai ki Ngākau Hihiko mō te kōrero, te hononga me te whakakaha i ngā wāhine o te rāngai pūngao.

There’s nothing quite like getting a great group of wāhine in energy together in one room.

Join Ngākau Hihiko – Wāhine in Energy and our hosts Octopus Energy for an evening of connection, conversation and networking, featuring a relaxed fireside chat with Emelye Rooney, facilitated by Idil Kaplan.

Emelye has built her career in the energy industry, progressing from operational leadership at Octopus Energy into technology client delivery at Kraken Technologies. She is passionate about people, leadership and workplace culture and has shared her experiences with leaders and emerging talent internationally. This includes speaking with teams at Octopus Energy Japan about psychological safety and building high-performing cultures, as well as facilitating Kraken's onboarding programme across Melbourne and London.

Come along, meet some new people, reconnect with familiar faces and find out more about Ngākau Hihiko and the community we’re building.


Doors open at 5:30pm. Please arrive by 5:50pm, as building access is restricted after 5:30pm and the formal programme will begin promptly at 6:00pm

Wine, watercolours and wonderful views – what better way to spend a day?

Watercolour at Spy Valley Winery – Art, Wine & Lunch

Looking for something a little different? Join us at Spy Valley Winery for a day of watercolour painting, wine tasting and good food in the beautiful Marlborough countryside.

We'll set up in a spacious private boardroom overlooking the vineyards, with sweeping panoramic views towards the dramatic Richmond Ranges and Wither Hills, right in the heart of the Waihopai Valley.

Whether you're new to watercolour or already enjoy painting, everyone is welcome. No experience is necessary – just bring your curiosity and we'll guide you through the day.

Come along, try something new, enjoy some wonderful wine and spend a day painting in one of Marlborough's most beautiful settings.

Spaces are limited, so get in touch to book your place!

name: Manawa Ora Mirimiri - The Foundations of Māori Healing & Bodywork
venue:

Wellington, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview

Experience traditional Māori healing practices grounded in cultural knowledge in this 2-day Foundational workshop with Manawa Ora

Nau mai, haere mai ki Manawa Ora – The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork.

We invite you to reconnect with the wisdom of our tūpuna and explore the foundations of traditional Māori healing through a holistic, hands-on approach to wellbeing. Grounded in mātauranga Māori, this workshop provides an introduction to the principles, values and practices that underpin Māori healing.

Throughout this workshop, participants will be introduced to mirimiri and romiromi (Māori bodywork), exploring intention and connection in the healing process. We will consider cultural aspects such as whakapapa, tikanga, manaakitanga and wairuatanga.

The workshop offers a supportive space to learn, reflect and develop an awareness of how Māori healing traditions can inform our approach to wellbeing, both for ourselves and for those we care for. Participants will be encouraged to pay attention to their own bodies, deepen their connection with others and appreciate the responsibility that comes with engaging in the healing process.

Over the last 10 years, these workshops have welcomed people from all races and backgrounds. Wānanga/workshops are safe spaces for people to come together for the pupose of learning and healing, guided by tikanga.

At Manawa Ora, we believe that healing begins with connection – connection to ourselves, to one another, to our whakapapa and to the ancient knowledge of Rongoā Māori passed down through generations.

Whether you are beginning your journey into Māori healing or seeking to strengthen your existing understanding, this workshop provides a foundation from which to grow with respect, aroha and intention.

PLEASE NOTE THIS WORKSHOP IS NOT A QUALIFICATION TO PRACTICE.

The 2-day workshop includes:

Cultural philosophies
Whatumanawa (intuitive diagnosis)
Self-awareness and insight
Waiata, karakia and takutaku
Spiritual hygiene
Introduction to mirimiri and romiromi
Group interaction & hands-on practice
Selfcare and tools to maintain wellness

Facilitator Jolie Davis has over 30 years experience in Rongoā Māori; mirimiri and romiromi. Educator, advocate, founder and lead practitioner at Manawa Ora, the largest provider of Rongoā Māori in the Wellington region and one of the largest in Aotearoa (NZ).

WHO THIS WĀNANGA IS FOR:

This wānanga welcomes all with an open heart and an open mind

Individuals on a personal healing journey, ready to discover their inner potential
Māori and Kiwis living overseas seeking reconnection with whakapapa, culture and self-identity.
Those drawn to indigenous healing modalities and philosophy.
Bodyworkers, healers and mainstream practitioners seeking to expand their knowledge and practice

Register at: https://form.jotform.com/joliedavis/Manawaora-Dec2026

Or email joliedavis@manawaora.org for payment options.

long_description:
Overview

Come along to this final Think Well Corner session for 2026 and learn how to think clearly, respond wisely and protect your peace of mind.

We've all met them. The colleague who pushes our buttons, the person who always has something negative to say, or someone who somehow manages to turn an ordinary interaction into a difficult one.

And while we can't always change how other people behave, we can become much smarter about how we think about them, how we respond and how much energy we give them.

Join us for a practical, down-to-earth session exploring three simple ways to deal with difficult people more effectively:

1. Question your thinking

Are you seeing the situation clearly, or making assumptions about someone's intentions and behaviour?

2. Choose your response

Learn how to step back, avoid reacting on autopilot and respond in ways that are more constructive.

3. Protect your energy

Understand when to address difficult behaviour, establish boundaries or simply let things go.

And we'll turn the question around too: What if I'm the difficult person? A little self-awareness can go a long way!

There'll be practical examples, useful ideas and plenty of opportunity for discussion.

The aim? To leave with a few simple thinking tools you can put to use in everyday life.

Because you can't always choose the people you meet along the way, but you can choose how you respond to them.

THINK WELL CORNER

Practical thinking skills for real life.

Saturday 28 November

Wellington Central Library – Hui 4

0800 BE OPEN
